MUQATIL:70:19-35/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:70:19-35/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:70:19-35/r2.claim: Worshippers are excepted from the human traits of anxiety and miserliness.

FARRA:v3p185/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p185/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p185/r4.claim: The exception of worshippers is from the generic, collective sense of “the human,” as believers are excepted from humanity's loss.

TUSTARI:70:22/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:70:22/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:70:22/r1.claim: The worshippers are people of gnosis who recognize the value of things: they rejoice only in God, find rest only in Him, and grieve at separation from Him.

TUSTARI:70:22/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:70:22/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:70:22/r2.claim: A report describes the best of the Prophet’s community as people who laugh openly at God’s broad mercy yet weep privately from fear of His punishment, remember and supplicate to Him, long for Him, burden others lightly, and discipline themselves.

NAHHAS:v5p31/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p31/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p31/r2.claim: Al-muṣallīn is accusative as an exception.

SULAMI:v2p350#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r1.claim: The restless person despairs in poverty and withholds when wealthy; the enabled worshippers are excepted.

SULAMI:v2p350#6/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r2.claim: The praying ones are gnostics who know the worth of things and find relief and rest only in God.

SULAMI:v2p350#6/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r3.claim: Despair reflects ignorance of God's apportionment, while withholding is a trait of hypocrites.

SULAMI:v2p350#6/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r4.claim: The praying ones do not panic because they trust their Lord and His decree.

SULAMI:v2p350#6/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r5.claim: When they hear useful knowledge or righteous deeds, their hearts long for them.

SULAMI:v2p350#6/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p350#6/r6.claim: When a person commits an indecency or sin, ignorance of repentance leads to despair.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r10.claim: Those constant in prayer guard the appointed times of obligatory prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r11.claim: Those constant in prayer perform many voluntary prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r12.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p94/r12.claim: Those constant in prayer do not turn their attention away during it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p224/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p224/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p224/r1.claim: The plural worshippers are excepted from singular ‘the human’ because الإنسان has collective meaning, as in the exception for believers in al-Asr.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p363#4/r1.claim: The exception means believers who pray; a plural group can be excepted from al-insān because it is a collective generic noun.

RAZI-FULL:v30p114#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p114#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p114#2/r1.claim: Being constant in prayer means never omitting it; guarding prayer in 70:34 means attending to its excellence and proper performance.

RAZI-FULL:v30p114#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p114#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p114#2/r2.claim: Care for prayer spans preparation, performance, and what follows: prepare for its time, ablution, covering, direction, purity, congregation, and focus; attend to recitation and remembrance; then avoid idle activity and sins.

RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p114/r3.claim: The exception begins by describing the praying people as constant in prayer; the passage says there are eight qualities and continues the list.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r2.speaker: النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r2.claim: Al-Nakha‘i identifies those who pray as people who perform the obligatory prayer.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says they observe prayer at its prescribed time, and abandoning prayer is unbelief.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:22-33/r4.claim: Other interpretations identify them as the Companions or believers generally, who overcome panic through trust in God and certainty.

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:22-27/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:22-27/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:22-27/r1.claim: The exception singles out worshippers who oppose greed by obeying God, caring for others, believing in judgment, fearing punishment, curbing desire, and preferring the lasting future.

QASHANI:70:22-23/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:70:22-23/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:70:22-23/r1.claim: The exception is for those who strive fully, shed ego qualities, and reach direct witnessing; continuous prayer is the soul’s enduring contemplation, eclipsing all besides the witnessed.

QASHANI:70:22-23/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:70:22-23/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:70:22-23/r2.claim: The detached also relinquish outward and inward wealth, including useful true knowledge, distributing it to prepared seekers and those prevented from seeking by distractions.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p275/r2.claim: Except the people of prayer is an exception from humankind, and they are characterized by patience in hardship and the noble traits that follow.

SAMIN-DURR:70:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:22/r1.claim: The exception is from generic ‘the human’; the author compares the construction with the exception in the closing verses of al-‘Asr.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p226/r4.claim: The exception is those God protects and guides: worshippers who maintain their prayers.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r1.claim: The exception identifies those who maintain prayer: their worship restrains the haluʿ nature so that neither their distress nor withholding becomes extreme, and they act to please God.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r2.claim: God equips them to refine their nature through good companions, admonition, avoiding corrupt places and company, and habits that prompt noble conduct; preserving religious limits despite contrary impulses is a great honor.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p150/r3.claim: The eight qualities that follow correspond to the eight gates of Paradise and complete faith's two halves, patience and gratitude.

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r10.claim: Qatada says Daniel described Muhammad's community as praying in a way that would have saved earlier peoples from their disasters; prayer is a fine believer's trait.

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r11.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r11.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says those constant in prayer maintain the obligatory prayers.

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r12.claim: Ibn Masud says constancy in prayer means keeping its appointed times; Masruq reports the same.

DURR-FULL:v8p283/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r13.speaker: عمران بن حصين
DURR-FULL:v8p283/r13.claim: Imran ibn Husayn says the constant worshipper does not look around during prayer.

BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r3.claim: Worshippers are excepted from humankind understood collectively because they transform blameworthy traits; the fronted ‘they’ strengthens the claim that they persist in prayer.

BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r4.speaker: عائشة
BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet’s practice was steady; the Prophet called the most excellent deed the most constant even if small.

BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r5.claim: Prayer is first obligation and reckoning, remains required even when illness excuses fasting, and was the Prophet’s final counsel.

BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p124#2/r6.claim: Inwardly, the soul’s prayer purifies from forbidden acts, the heart’s from worldly desire, the secret’s from high stations, the spirit’s uses divine unveiling, and the hidden prayer is annihilation in God.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p62#4/r1.claim: Worshippers are purified from panic through full obedience to God, compassion for people, belief in judgment, fear of punishment, restraint of desire, and choosing the hereafter over worldly gain.

ELMALILI:70:8-35/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r13.claim: Believing people who pray are exempt from this bad character, torment, and evil end, and are honored in gardens through the virtues that follow.

TABATABAI:70:22-27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:22-27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:22-27/r1.claim: The worshippers are excepted from the human described as panicked; placing prayer first among the listed good works signals its rank and its strong effect against blameworthy greed.

TABATABAI:70:22-27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:22-27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:22-27/r2.claim: Prayer restrains the shameful conduct and wrongdoing associated with this vice, as the author links the verse to 29:45.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r8.claim: People generally become frustrated and complain when God punishes them even a little for their deeds.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r1.claim: The cure for human impatience and selfishness is strong responsibility grounded in belief in the afterlife, expressed through worship and constructive moral conduct.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r2.claim: The passage lists regular prayer, giving the poor their due, concern for the afterlife, chastity, fidelity to trusts, and truthful testimony as examples of good conduct.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:22/r3.claim: These virtues are illustrative rather than exhaustive; their number varies with circumstances, while the aim is to resist impatience, ingratitude, and selfishness and enrich character.

STUDYQURAN:70:19/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r4.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:70:19/r4.claim: Because the passage exempts those who pray, it suggests that the traits describe humanity broadly.

STUDYQURAN:70:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:22/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:70:22/r1.claim: Like 23:1–11, this thorough list presents Islam’s moral and ritual duties; 23:3 adds turning away from idle talk, and 33:35 is another parallel.

STUDYQURAN:70:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:22/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:70:22/r2.claim: Constancy in prayer may mean performing the prescribed rites without neglect, as in 70:34, or simply praying all five daily prayers.

STUDYQURAN:70:22/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:22/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:70:22/r20.claim: The list begins and ends with prayer, showing prayer’s central place among religious acts.

STUDYQURAN:70:22/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:22/r3.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:70:22/r3.claim: The phrase may also mean maintaining prayer of the heart at all times.
